speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed description. To differentiate this from night terrors, does she have a dream-like recall of what was happening when she wakes up? text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Patient
text: No significant findings in other systems. No history of trauma or significant stress identified. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: This diagnosis is clinically inconsistent with the provided history of sleep disturbances and lack of daytime symptoms; the mention of Pyelonephritis appears to be a medical error by the previous provider. Based on the child's age, frequency of frightened awakening with dream recall, and ability to be consoled, this is most consistent with REM Sleep Behavior Disorder or Night Terrors. No further tests are required at this time.
